method: every round runs the program at N churns and then at 0 churns back to back, and ns/op is the median paired difference (wall@N - wall@0) / N * 1e6 — never two separate means, whose difference absorbs a drifting boot cost instead of cancelling it. note: the op count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load. Whether a runtime's collector actually runs during the loop is its own admission policy — this row measures the allocate-and-abandon wall time, and claims no collection count

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: A gross-regression alarm for the Rust boot median (the m17 rounds read 289-546 ms under a 1-min load of 3-92; quieter sessions read ~280-400 ms), not an SLO — a shared host can double it without a code change, so the load-robust judgement is the rust/sys ratio row.

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: Catches a hang or an order-of-magnitude tail regression (the matched m17 rounds read 291-485 ms p99, with a single 1702 ms outlier on a heavily loaded A/B round), not an SLO: a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so this row only notices a gross failure.

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: The load-robust startup judgement: recorded matched-round ratios are 2.2-3.05x (m16 reached 3.79x), so 6x is a regression alarm with headroom above every recorded round — not a target, and deliberately not so tight that ordinary host drift trips it.

budgets.reason: no `rust` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: The same instrument for the tail; recorded p99 ratios track the p50 ones (2.1-3.4x) because a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so the same 6x alarm applies — not an SLO for a shared host.

The oracle's own tail, recorded at 105-153 ms across m17: a host artifact big enough to move the far less load-sensitive `sys` side shows up here too, so it cannot be misread as a Rust regression — and 400 ms is deliberately loose because this row exists to attribute, not to gate.
